subject: Atlas AI — budget range, expected tokens & peak concurrency (post-demo)
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodai.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@atlasai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodai.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Atlas AI — budget range, expected tokens & peak concurrency (post-demo)

Samir — great call today, thanks for walking us through the Atlas AI product flows. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we can move pricing/PO along: 

Summary of what you shared (please confirm):
- Primary use case: in-chat assistant + nightly batch summarization for support tickets.
- Expected steady-state monthly tokens: 120M–260M tokens/month (we heard ~200M midpoint).
- Campaign spikes: live marketing campaigns will introduce short bursts and a peak TPS target of ~320 TPS for 5–10 minute windows (estimated 2–3x baseline).
- Budget target: mid-stage procurement target ~$9k–$28k/month (you said range is flexible depending on SLA & burst support).

What I recommended on the call (and what we'll propose formally):
- Hosted API price-band recommendation (ballpark): $8–$12 per 1M tokens at 100M+ volumes depending on concurrency guarantees and KV cache reuse.
- Burst handling: include a burst overlay (pay-as-you-go burst capacity) or reserved burst slab for repeat campaigns — preserves latency SLO without full reserved capacity.
- Next technical step: 30m infra sizing call with one of our runtime engineers to validate the 320 TPS 99th percentile behavior and confirm KV cache expectations.

Actions / asks for Atlas AI:
1) Confirm the monthly token range above (steady-state min / expected / max).
2) Share a 72-hour sample export (or the CSV we referenced) of average qps and 99th percentile request size so our infra team can validate latency targets. (If you can’t share production data, an anonymized sample is fine.)
3) Confirm procurement timeline and whether a PO is handled by Dana (cc’d).

Attached: redwood-pricing-bands-v2.pdf (pricing bands + example scenarios), mvp-traffic-telemetry.csv (example template).

I’ll draft a short proposal after you confirm volumes — should be quick. Availability for the infra call: Thu 2/11 10–11am PT or Mon 2/15 9–11am PT.

Thanks,
Vivek
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-pricing-bands-v2.pdf (PDF, 3 pages), mvp-traffic-telemetry.csv (CSV, template)

From: Samir Patel <samir@atlasai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Dana Lee <dana@atlasai.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Atlas AI — budget range, expected tokens & peak concurrency (post-demo)

Thanks Vivek — this is a useful recap. A few clarifications below.

Confirmed numbers:
- Steady-state: targeting ~180M tokens/month in Q2, expect to cross to ~240M by Q4 if growth goes well.
- Spikes: 320 TPS is our worst-case for marketing bursts; nominal baseline TPS sits around 90–110 TPS. Spikes last ~5–12 minutes and are highly bursty.
- Budget: procurement target is $10k–$25k/month.

Questions from our infra/Product side:
1) How does Redwood measure the 99th percentile for model-facing latency? For the bursts we care most about the 99.9th tail.
2) If we opt for hosted with a reserved burst slab, what is the expected delta in $/1M tokens versus pure pay-as-you-go during campaigns?

Dana — can you confirm procurement timeline? We’re hoping to finalize vendor selection within the next 3 weeks.

On sharing telemetry: I can send a 48–72h anonymized sample of request sizes and timestamps by EOD Friday.

—Samir
CTO, Atlas AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodai.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@atlasai.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Atlas AI — budget range, expected tokens & peak concurrency (post-demo)

Samir — thanks for the numbers, and appreciate the telemetry offer. A couple of concrete notes so procurement/Dana has something to review: 

Pricing (illustrative bands, final will be in the proposal):
- Band A (100–150M/mo): $11.00 per 1M tokens; pay-as-you-go bursts at +25% premium.
- Band B (150–250M/mo): $9.00 per 1M tokens; pay-as-you-go bursts at +18% premium.
- Band C (250M+): $7.50 per 1M tokens; reserved burst slab pricing negotiable.

Operational notes:
- For short marketing bursts (5–12m windows) we recommend enabling prefix/KV caching and a 2-tier fallback policy so non-critical calls can be routed to a cheaper compatible variant if capacity gets constrained. That preserves median latency and reduces unit cost.
- 99.9th percentile: our runtime measures tail latency at the request layer (model-run + queuing) and reports 50/90/99/99.9 in the Console. For the campaign profile you described, we typically see tail amplification when sequence lengths vary widely; the infra sizing call will let us validate our 99.9th predictions against your sample.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Technical sizing call (30m) — Tue 2/16 10:30am PT with our infra engineer Ben.
2) Samir to upload anonymized 48–72h telemetry to the Drive link; Marissa will run a quick pre-check and return a sizing note.
3) Vivek will send a formal proposal and a short SOW draft targeted to procurement.

If PO goes through quickly we can start onboarding within 2–3 weeks; otherwise pay-as-you-go is available immediately.

Cheers,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
